quiz_metadata.title: General Tagalog Grammar & Theory Master Quiz

questions.prompt: Which article is used before a singular proper name of a person?
questions.explanation: 'Si' is used before a singular proper noun of a person (e.g. Si Liza ay babae).

questions.prompt: Which article marker is used before two or more proper names of people?
questions.explanation: 'Sina' is the plural proper noun article used before two or more names (e.g. Sina Simon at Tom).

questions.prompt: Translate 'The house is big' into Inverted / Transposed Word Order (without 'ay'): ______
questions.explanation: In inverted word order, the predicate (adjective) comes first, followed by the subject, dropping 'ay'.

questions.prompt: What is the plural form of the adjective 'mabait' (kind)?
questions.explanation: Adjectives form their plural by duplicating the first syllable of the root word (root: bait -> mababait).

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between 'kami' and 'tayo'?
options: 'kami' excludes the listener; 'tayo' includes the listener
'kami' includes the listener; 'tayo' excludes the listener
questions.correct_answer: 'kami' excludes the listener; 'tayo' includes the listener
questions.explanation: 'Kami' is exclusive we (excludes the listener), while 'tayo' is inclusive we (includes speaker and listener).

questions.prompt: When placing the 2nd person singular pronoun after the predicate in inverted order, which form is used?
questions.explanation: 'Ikaw' is used at the beginning of a sentence. After the predicate in inverted order, it shortens to 'ka' (e.g. Marunong ka).

questions.prompt: How do you ask 'Are you a teacher, sir/madam?' respectfully using the polite pronoun: ______ po ba ay guro?
questions.explanation: Plural pronouns 'Kayo' or 'Sila' combined with 'po' express politeness when addressing a single person.

questions.prompt: Which demonstrative pronoun refers to an object far from both the speaker and the listener?
questions.explanation: 'Ito' = near speaker; 'Iyan' = near listener; 'Iyon' = far from both speaker and listener.

questions.prompt: Which ligature suffix is attached to words ending in vowels (a, e, i, o, u)?
questions.explanation: Words ending in vowels take the suffix ligature '-ng' (e.g. malaki + bahay -> malaking bahay).

questions.prompt: Which ligature suffix is attached to words ending in the consonant 'n'?
questions.explanation: Words ending in the consonant 'n' take the suffix ligature '-g' (e.g. mayaman + lalaki -> mayamang lalaki).

questions.prompt: Which ligature word is used when the first word ends in consonants other than 'n'?
questions.explanation: Between words where the first ends in consonants other than 'n', the ligature word 'na' is used (e.g. tahimik na bata).

questions.prompt: Complete the phrase for 'Maria's house': ang bahay ___ Maria
questions.explanation: 'Ni' is placed before singular proper names of people to indicate possession.

questions.prompt: Complete the phrase for 'the teacher's pencil': ang lapis ___ guro
questions.explanation: 'Ng' (pronounced nangg) is placed before common nouns to indicate possession.

questions.prompt: In Tagalog possessive expressions, which element MUST come first?
options: The possessed object comes before the owner
The owner comes before the possessed object
The adjective comes after the owner
questions.correct_answer: The possessed object comes before the owner
questions.explanation: In Tagalog possessive constructions, the possessed object ALWAYS precedes the owner (e.g. ang bahay ni Maria).

questions.prompt: What is the post-noun possessive pronoun form corresponding to the 1st person singular base 'akin'?
questions.explanation: Base pre-noun 'akin' (with ligature 'aking') changes to 'ko' when placed after the noun (e.g. ang bahay ko).

questions.prompt: What is the post-noun possessive pronoun form corresponding to 2nd person singular 'iyo'?
questions.explanation: Base pre-noun 'iyo' (with ligature 'iyong') changes to 'mo' when placed after the noun (e.g. ang baro mo).

questions.prompt: Which demonstrative possessive word means 'of this person' (near speaker)?
questions.explanation: 'Nito' is the possessive form of 'ito' (of this person near speaker). 'Niyan' = near listener, 'Niyon' = far from both.

questions.prompt: What prefix pattern forms the present (ongoing) tense for nag- verbs?
options: nag- + duplicated first syllable of root + root
mag- + duplicated first syllable of root + root
questions.correct_answer: nag- + duplicated first syllable of root + root
questions.explanation: Present (ongoing) aspect duplicates the first syllable of the root after 'nag-' (e.g. laro -> naglalaro).

questions.prompt: What is the future tense form of the verb root 'laro' (to play)? ______
questions.explanation: Future (contemplated) aspect uses 'mag-' + duplicated first syllable of root (maglalaro).

questions.prompt: The sentence linker 'ay' can be shortened to ''y' when the preceding word ends in what sound?
questions.explanation: The linker 'ay' contracts to ''y' when the preceding word ends in a vowel (e.g. Ako ay -> Ako'y).
